turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Thank you. Um, well, what finally pushed me to actually come in is... work. I'm a health services manager, and I can start an EPIC quality report, or, you know, sit down in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking what's going on. But within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far that I’m just rereading the same numbers over and over. 

Which is honestly so frustrating right now because EPIC just had this massive system update, right? And the new dashboard is completely counterintuitive. I was telling my sister about it—she works in healthcare administration too, over at Memorial—and she said her hospital actually refused to update their system because of exactly this issue. We had an IT guy in last week, Greg I think, and he spent half the afternoon just trying to fix the drop-down menus for the nursing staff. He was telling me about his golden retriever having knee surgery, which sounded so expensive... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Oh. Right. The reports. The point is, I'll be looking at these screens or sitting in these metric reviews, and I'll suddenly realize I've completely missed the whole point of the discussion. My brain just goes somewhere else entirely.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly describes an inability to sustain attention during tasks like reading reports or sitting in meetings, noting their mind drifts within minutes.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient demonstrates tangential speech during the response, drifting from work reports to a software update, their sister, an IT worker, and a dog's knee surgery before losing their train of thought.

Like, my husband and I just started watching this new baking competition on Netflix. The one where they make those massive chocolate sculptures? It is just amazing what they can do with modeling chocolate. I actually tried making a layered chocolate cake for my niece's birthday last month—she just turned 12, which is terrifying because I swear she was just a toddler yesterday—and the frosting completely melted everywhere because I didn't let the cake cool long enough. My kitchen was an absolute disaster. My husband had to spend an hour scrubbing the granite... 

But, um, I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I don't know. I haven't really noticed it happening with friends or at home. It's really just the work stuff that's standing out to me right now.

The ad had this really sad video of a sea turtle, and I just felt awful. So I bought a six-month supply, but honestly, they don't get the smells out of my husband's gym clothes at all. He plays in this men's recreational basketball league on Tuesday nights, and I swear, the guys on his team take it way too seriously. One of them actually twisted his ankle last week because he tried to dunk—he's like 45, he has no business trying to dunk! School years? Oh, wow, that feels like a lifetime ago. Um, yeah, I think it's always been there. Even back in elementary school, I remember my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. They used that word a lot—careless. And my mother, bless her heart, she used to have to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night while I did my homework. The kitchen table was this big, heavy oak thing that my parents bought at an estate sale before I was born. It had these huge claw feet, and I used to pretend they were dragon claws when I was little. I actually saw a table just like it on an antique appraisal show the other night. I love watching those shows, it's so fascinating what people just have sitting in their attics. This one lady brought in a vase she bought at a garage sale for two dollars, and it turned out to be worth like fifty thousand dollars! Can you imagine? I should really go through the boxes in my garage, but it's so hot in there right now...

Wait, sorry. School. Right. Um, yeah, my mom had to sit with me because I was always losing track of my assignments or I'd forget my books at school. So, no, it's not a new thing. It's pretty much always been like this, I guess.
